hero.kicker: SEMI-FINAL EVE · BASTILLE DAY IN DALLAS
hero.headline: THE FINAL, ARRIVING A ROUND EARLY.
hero.standfirst: No football today — just the calm before the collision. France arrive in Dallas as the tournament's only perfect team, six wins from six. Spain arrive with the meanest defence in World Cup history and the receipts from Euro 2024, when Lamine Yamal and Dani Olmo knocked France out at this exact stage. Tomorrow night, 21:00 our time, one of them books the MetLife final.
hero.photoCaption: Kylian Mbappé — "completely fine", and one win from a third World Cup final on Bastille Day

briefing.text: Mbappé trained and declared himself "completely fine" after the ankle knock from Diop in the quarter-final. Tchouaméni's groin remains France's one real doubt.
England are healthy again: Rice is over the illness that wrecked his quarter-final, and Henderson — broken arm and all — stays in the squad. Messi shook off the knock to the face from Xhaka.
The Crystal Ball rests today and returns tomorrow morning with the France–Spain call, live market prices and the full factor grid.

today.preview: France on Bastille Day: six wins from six, one goal conceded, and Mbappé passing his fitness test with a shrug — "completely fine." The doubt is Tchouaméni's groin. Spain counter with the defence that went six straight games without conceding, a World Cup record, and with Yamal — who ended France's Euro 2024 at this same stage, aged 16. The money leans French at 42%, but 30% sits on the draw: the market smells extra time.

keyMan.name: Lamine Yamal
keyMan.line: He ended France's Euro 2024 in this exact fixture, aged 16, and added a brace on them in the 2025 Nations League semi. France still haven't solved him.

today.preview: The Hand of God, Beckham's red, Beckham's penalty — and now a World Cup semi-final. Both squads report clean bills of health: Rice has shaken off his illness, Messi the knock to the face from Xhaka, and Henderson stays around the squad with his arm in a cast. Both played 120 minutes Saturday, so recovery is the week's real contest. The market still can't split them: England 37, the draw 33, Argentina 31.

keyMan.name: Harry Kane
keyMan.line: Five goals, and the big-stage final third is where he lives. England have never beaten Argentina in a World Cup knockout without him scoring — he intends to keep it that way.
